articles.title: How to set a CI budget for coding agents
articles.excerpt: A CI budget for coding agents needs three layers: a time limit on every job, a rule that cancels runs the agent already superseded, and a hard dollar stop that refuses new work once it is reached. Git…
articles.body: A CI budget for coding agents needs three layers: a time limit on every job, a rule that cancels runs the agent already superseded, and a hard dollar stop that refuses new work once it is reached. GitHub gives you the first two in YAML and the third as an account or repository budget; Latchkey adds a budget on each piece of work, a batch, under a workspace spend limit. Each layer catches what the one above lets through. The GitHub dollar stop covers an account or repository; Latchkey adds one per piece of work. The expensive failure is rarely one big job. It is a cheap job repeated: a test the agent cannot fix, a hang it does not notice, a push per attempt that starts the full pipeline each time. Nobody is watching at 3 a.m., and an agent does not get bored.

On v7, authenticate with a repository token, with use_oidc: true and id-token: write , or tokenless where Codecov allows it, and set fail_ci_if_error: true , because by default a failed upload leaves the job green. The credential order in action.yml at v7.1.1, and what Codecov does with an upload that has none. Every failure after it is soft unless fail_ci_if_error is true. The Codecov step is usually the last line of a test job and the one nobody looks at.

articles.title: GitHub Actions cache not restored: the four silent misses
articles.excerpt: A GitHub Actions cache not restored is almost never a broken cache service. It is one of four things: a key that is different on every run, a restore-key prefix that matched an entry you did not want,…
articles.body: A GitHub Actions cache not restored is almost never a broken cache service. It is one of four things: a key that is different on every run, a restore-key prefix that matched an entry you did not want, nothing saved anywhere this branch can read, or a save the service refused. All four exit zero. The four misses and the line each one prints. Strings quoted from the actions/cache and actions/toolkit sources, read on 2026-09-20. What this error means The install step that a cache was supposed to shorten runs at full length, and nothing in the job is marked failed. The evidence is one line, either in the restore step or in the post-job step, and the exit code is zero whichever line you got.

articles.body: Building Smarter Inventory Tracking Systems with RFID and IoT Inventory tracking sounds simple until a business starts managing thousands of products across multiple storage locations. At a small scale, spreadsheets and barcode scanners might be enough. But as inventory volumes increase, keeping records accurate and updated becomes more challenging. Products move between locations, employees handle multiple orders, and information needs to be shared across different systems. This is where technologies such as RFID and the Internet of Things (IoT) become interesting from a software development perspective. They provide new ways to collect inventory information and connect physical warehouse activities with digital systems.

articles.title: Claude works in the browser but Claude Code can't connect: a 7-step proxy checklist
articles.excerpt: If claude.ai loads in your browser but Claude Code times out in the terminal, the browser is using your system proxy and the CLI is not. Claude Code is a terminal process and only reads proxy environm…
articles.body: If claude.ai loads in your browser but Claude Code times out in the terminal, the browser is using your system proxy and the CLI is not. Claude Code is a terminal process and only reads proxy environment variables. In almost every case the cause is one of three things. The variable is not set in the shell that launched it, the address is a SOCKS address, or NO_PROXY is excluding the request. Each step below gives you an answer in under a minute. Facts come from the official Claude Code network configuration page, checked on 15 November 2026. 1. Find your local HTTP port Open the settings of Clash Verge Rev, FlClash or whatever client you run and look for the HTTP port or mixed port. 7890 and 7897 are common. Use the number your own client shows. A subscription URL is not a proxy address.

articles.body: On Episode 236 of This Week In Space , Tariq Malik and Rod Pyle are joined by Mikhail Tikhonov to talk about how life can take more unusual forms, ones we might not even recognize. When we think of extraterrestrials, our minds generally go from the latex-suited bipedal aliens seen in Star Trek and Star Wars to more exotic critters in sci-fi movies. Scientists think in terms of carbon-based microbial life and other lower life forms. But some researchers, such as Tikhonov from Washington University, suggest that life can take more unusual forms, ones we might not even recognize. He further suggests a new definition of life: something that takes in and transforms energy and replicates. His ideas radically expand our notions of alien life and how it might be recognized.

articles.excerpt: SpaceX is looking into why its latest Starship megarocket test flight missed the first of two planned landings on Friday (Nov. 13) during the Starship Flight 15 test.
articles.body: Update for 3:40 p.m. ET on Nov. 14: SpaceX's Kate Tice provided more information about the booster abort at about 3:30 p.m. EST (1830 GMT) on Nov. 14, during the company's Flight 15 webcast. "Early indications are that the booster ended its boostback [burn] early due to a low fuel mass alarm," she said. "The team is still investigating the root cause on that." SpaceX is looking into why its latest Starship megarocket test flight missed the first of two planned landings on Friday (Nov. 13), triggering an automatic abort that destroyed the booster. The giant Starship rocket , a massive two-stage vehicle that's the largest launcher on Earth, soared into orbit from SpaceX's Starbase in South Texas on Friday on the company's ambitious Flight 15 test flight.

articles.title: On this day in space! Nov. 14, 1969: NASA's Apollo 12 astronauts launch to the moon on a 'pinpoint landing' lunar mission
articles.excerpt: On Nov. 14, 1969, the Apollo 12 astronauts launched to the moon. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Nov. 14, 1969, the Apollo 12 mission launched to the moon. This was the second moon landing of the Apollo program. The two astronauts on board were Pete Conrad , commander, and Alan Bean , the lunar module pilot. Astronaut Richard Gordon , the command module pilot, stayed in the command module and orbited the moon while his crewmates went to the surface. The astronauts made a pinpoint landing in a lunar mare called the Ocean of Storms. The previous moon mission, Apollo 11 , drifted far from the planned landing zone. But Apollo 12 landed close to a scientific target. That target was a robotic lander called Surveyor 3 . Scientists wanted to look at Surveyor 3 to see how well the spacecraft lasted on the moon since it landed there more than two years earlier.
